# Vendored librespot crates

Copies of published librespot 0.8.0 crates (MIT licensed, see `LICENSE` in each
directory), wired into the build through `[patch.crates-io]` in
`native/Cargo.toml`. Every local change is marked with a `// SPOTIFYGOOD:`
comment so the patch can be re-applied when upgrading librespot.

| Crate | Why it is vendored |
|-------|--------------------|
| `librespot-core` | Stock `Session::check_catalogue` calls `std::process::exit(1)` for non-Premium accounts, which would kill the Android app. It is patched to report the error and shut the session down instead. |
| `librespot-connect` | The stock crate keeps the Connect state private. The app needs to read the queue and context, edit the queue locally, see the other Connect devices in the account, and implement smart shuffle. |
| `librespot-playback` | Offline playback of downloaded (still encrypted) tracks needs a hook in the track loader; the stock player also calls `exit(1)` on sink errors, gives no way to tell refused audio keys apart, and runs one tokio worker per CPU core. See `librespot-playback/PATCHES.md`. |

## Patches

`grep -rn SPOTIFYGOOD native/vendor` lists every change. Files that are entirely
new say so in their first line.

### librespot-core

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `src/session.rs` | `check_catalogue` is now a method. For a non-Premium `type` attribute it records `SessionInvalidReason::NonPremiumAccount { account_type }` and calls `Session::shutdown()` instead of `std::process::exit(1)`. It covers the ProductInfo packet and `set_user_attribute(s)`. Adds `pub enum SessionInvalidReason` (`#[non_exhaustive]`) and `pub fn Session::invalid_reason(&self) -> Option<SessionInvalidReason>`. Removes the `process::exit` import. | `exit(1)` would kill the Android app and its foreground service without any UI. |
| `src/config.rs` | `pub const OS: &str = "linux"` (was `std::env::consts::OS`). `os_version()` falls back to `"6.1"` when sysinfo returns nothing or an empty string (was `"0"`). | On `target_os = "android"`, librespot presents the Android-app identity, and Spotify rejects that identity for keymaster-minted credentials. Every platform branch in core matches on this const, so the whole crate now presents the Linux desktop identity: the default client id is keymaster (`SessionConfig::default`, login5), the client-token platform data is `desktop_linux`, the user agent is `Spotify/<desktop version> Linux/0`, the AP handshake uses `PLATFORM_LINUX_*` / `OS_LINUX`, and `spotify_version()` is the desktop one. There are no direct `cfg(target_os)` or `consts::OS` uses in core. Consequence: `Login5Manager::login` (password login) returns `OnlyForMobile`, which the app doesn't use. spotify-player's Termux build applies the same patch. |
| `src/spclient.rs` | `pub fn RequestOptions::new(metrics: bool, salt: bool, base_url: Option<&'static str>) -> Self`. The fields stay private. | Without it, callers outside the crate can only use the default options with `request_with_options` (metrics and salt on). |
| `src/dealer/mod.rs` | In the reconnect loop, a failing `get_url()` (login5/apresolve) is logged, waits `RECONNECT_INTERVAL` (10 s) and retries, unless the dealer is closed. Before, the `?` ended the dealer for good. The connect-error sleep also aborts on close. | A transient token failure silently killed Connect for the rest of the session. `Dealer::close` no longer waits out the 10 s delay. |
| `src/audio_key.rs` | `AudioKeyError::AesKey { code: u16 }` (was a unit variant), parsed as a big-endian u16 from the `AesKeyError` payload after the sequence number, with no panic on a short payload. Display: `audio key error 0x0001`. Adds `pub const AES_KEY_ERROR_PERMANENT: u16 = 0x0001` and `AES_KEY_ERROR_TRANSIENT: u16 = 0x0002`. Code `0x0001` maps to `ErrorKind::PermissionDenied`, all other codes and `Timeout` map to `ErrorKind::Unavailable` (`Timeout` was `Aborted`). Adds `pub fn is_permanent_denial(err: &Error) -> bool`. The pending sender is removed on timeout and when sending the request fails (it leaked before). Adds a unit test. | Spotify refuses audio keys for some accounts (librespot #1649 / PR #1763). Callers (the vendored playback) need to tell "refused for this account" apart from throttling. |
| `src/dealer/protocol/request.rs` | **Unchanged.** serde ignores unknown fields (there is no `deny_unknown_fields` anywhere), so a `set_options` with extra fields such as `modes` still parses. A connect test covers this. Note that a present `options` object needs all three `OptionsOptions` bools. | Checked, no change needed. |

### librespot-connect

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `Cargo.toml` | tokio features `rt` and `time` are now listed. | `tokio::spawn` (suggestion fetches), `sleep` and `timeout`. Before, these only worked through feature unification with core. |
| `src/snapshot.rs` (new), `src/lib.rs` | Public read-only types `ConnectSnapshot` (with `ending`, see A), `SnapshotTrack`, `TrackProvider`, `SnapshotPlayStatus` and `SpircCommandError`. | The app needs the state, which upstream keeps private. |
| `src/state/snapshot.rs` (new) | `ConnectState::snapshot()` builds the snapshot. `snapshot_fingerprint()` is a cheap hash, so Spirc skips the rebuild when nothing visible changed. The position is hashed as its nominal start while playing, so re-anchoring on each PUT doesn't count as a change. | Snapshot stream (A). |
| `src/spirc.rs` | **A** `subscribe_state()`. A `watch` channel, published with `send_if_modified` at the bottom of every loop iteration and once in `Spirc::new`. The final snapshot, sent after the epilogue, has `ending: true` and is the state when the loop ended, before the epilogue's disconnect (a task that ended by itself would otherwise report "stopped, inactive" and hide what was playing). `is_running()` tells whether the task still takes commands. **B** `add_to_queue`, `remove_from_queue`, `move_queue_item`, `clear_queue`, `skip_to` (active only). `add_to_queue` fails right away (FailedPrecondition, `StateError::QueueFull`) when the queued tracks plus the adds not handled yet fill the 80 next tracks (a shared gauge, kept by the task); the task checks again, and the remote `add_to_queue` endpoint now fails instead of dropping the track. After every queue change, local or remote (`add_to_queue`/`set_queue`), and after shuffle changes, the next track is preloaded again if a preload had already been triggered. **C** `subscribe_cluster()` publishes `Option<Arc<Cluster>>` from the NEW_DEVICE PUT, from every cluster push, and from state/volume/audio-output PUT responses that parse as a cluster with devices. `refresh_cluster()` (allowed while inactive) puts the state to get a fresh cluster; a failure is only logged. **D** `smart_shuffle(bool)`. Suggestions are fetched off the loop (`tokio::spawn` + `get_autoplay_context` with about 20 sampled context track uris), at most one request at a time, and delivered back through a new `select!` arm. Results are dropped if the generation or context changed. Pacing: 30 s minimum between fetches, 5 min after an empty result, 30 s doubling to 10 min on errors, at most 40 pending suggestions. Suggestions are refetched after a load, a reshuffle, or a change to the default context through the resolver. **E** `set_audio_output(kind, name)`, allowed while inactive, PUTs with `AUDIO_DRIVER_INFO_CHANGED` only when the value changed. **F** Shutdown sets the flags first and never fails. The disconnect and the epilogue's DELETE and dealer close are each bounded by 3 s. A closed command channel (all handles dropped) is treated as shutdown, and a closed player event channel stops being polled (both were busy loops). Commands are now always polled: anything other than `Shutdown` that arrives before the connection is established is buffered, so an early shutdown no longer hangs. **G** `ConnectConfig.auto_takeover` gates the startup takeover. The takeover restores playback paused (`handle_transfer(.., start_paused)`). **I** `last_error` in the snapshot, plus `subscribe_errors()` (`broadcast`, capacity 16). Commands that are ignored while inactive now report `NotActive` (FailedPrecondition). **J** Cluster update without a cluster while active also stops the player. `prev` with repeat and no prev tracks loads the track. FilterExplicitContentChanged is emitted for both values. A remote `skip_next` to a uri that isn't in the next tracks falls back to a plain next, where before it consumed the queue, stopped playback, or never ended. **K** `set_autoplay(bool)` sets the local `autoplay` user attribute. It fails when `SessionConfig.autoplay` overrides it. Enabling queues an autoplay resolve; disabling drops pending autoplay resolves and the autoplay context unless autoplay is already playing. **L** `PlayerEvent::Unavailable` uses the reason: transient failures (`KeyTemporarilyDenied`, `NetworkError`) don't mark the track unavailable for the session (it is skipped, not blacklisted), and a failed preload only preloads the following track for track-specific reasons. After a key denial or a transient failure the chain of preloads walked the whole queue with one key request per track while a track played; that track is now loaded, and its failure handled, when the current one ends. | See the items in `connect.md` §15. |
| `src/state.rs` | `ConnectConfig.auto_takeover` (default false). `SPOTIFY_MAX_NEXT_TRACKS_SIZE` is `pub(crate)`, `StateError::QueueFull`. New state: `skipped_uids`, `smart_shuffle`, `suggestions`, `used_suggestion_uris`. `set_audio_output()` and `notify_audio_output_changed()`. `StateError::CanNotFindTrackInQueue`. `reset_playback_to_position` keeps a playing suggestion as the current track, like a queued one. | B, D, E, G |
| `src/state/handle.rs` | `queue_add_uri` (validated through `SpotifyUri`), `queue_remove`, `queue_clear`, `queue_move`, `clear_skipped_uids`, `has_playable_next_track`, `remove_autoplay_context`. Unshuffling clears smart shuffle. Repeat-context with a playing suggestion uses the position of the track it follows. Invariant: queued tracks stay contiguous at the front. | B, D, J, K |
| `src/state/tracks.rs` | `next_tracks_mut` is now `pub(super)`. `add_to_queue` returns `Result` and fails when 80 queued tracks fill the next tracks (the track was pushed and popped right away). Dropping the end of the next tracks (`add_to_queue`, `prev_track`) rewinds the fill up to the earliest dropped context or autoplay track (by uid, also when shuffled; a dropped delimiter wraps or transitions to autoplay again), so the dropped tracks are played later; upstream lost them. `prev_track` puts the old track and a delimiter back after the queued tracks, not in front of them. The fill up also skips uris marked unavailable after the context was loaded. Fill-up also skips `skipped_uids` and injects the suggestion after the context track at a suggestion position, only when the fill-up context is Default and the size cap allows. `prev_track` sets the index from the track's `context_index` instead of decrementing blindly. `skip_to_uid` is added. | B, D |
| `src/state/transfer.rs` | A transferred queue stops at the first track `add_to_queue` rejects (full queue). | B |
| `src/state/smart_shuffle.rs` (new) | Local smart shuffle. Suggestions are keyed by the position in the shuffled default context after which they are inserted (one after every 3rd context track) and are never added to `StateContext.tracks`, so unshuffle keeps working. They keep the `context` provider, carry the metadata `smart_shuffle.suggested=true`, and take the `context_index` of the track they follow. Already-suggested uris and uris of the context are filtered out. | D |
| `src/state/metadata.rs`, `src/state/options.rs`, `src/state/context.rs`, `src/model.rs` | Suggestion metadata key. `validate_shuffle_allowed` is now `pub(super)`. `reset_context(Completely)` clears the skipped uids and smart shuffle. `Options.smart_shuffle` (implies shuffle). `AudioOutputKind` maps to the proto `AudioOutputDeviceType`. | B, D, E |
| `src/context_resolver.rs` | The retry of unavailable contexts was dead code because the `duration_since` arguments were swapped; this is fixed. `RETRY_UNAVAILABLE` drops from 3600 s to 60 s. Adds `remove_autoplay()` and `next_update()`. | H, D, K |
| `src/state/tests.rs` (new) | Unit tests: queue invariants, skip-to, suggestion injection and the unshuffle round trip, smart shuffle off, snapshot mapping and clock, fingerprint stability, audio output, autoplay removal, tolerant `set_options` parsing, and a compile-time check that the task and handle are `Send`/`Sync`. | |

Notes for users of the connect patches:
- Snapshot clock: `position_timestamp_ms` is local epoch milliseconds (the same clock as `System.currentTimeMillis()`). The position now is `position_ms + (now - position_timestamp_ms) * playback_speed`, and `playback_speed` is 0 unless the status is `Playing`. Internally, Spirc puts server-corrected timestamps (`local + time_delta`).
- `next_tracks` and `prev_tracks` include hidden delimiters (`hidden == true`, uri `spotify:delimiter`). Filter them out for display.
- Only `subscribe_*`, `is_running`, `set_audio_output`, `set_autoplay`, `refresh_cluster`, `activate`, `transfer` and `shutdown` work while the device is inactive. Every other command reports a `NotActive` error. To control another device, use spclient directly.
- Smart shuffle is local. Other clients see the suggestions as ordinary context tracks, and the mode is not sent to Spotify (`modes` is not set).
